That record depends on `aiohttp-retry`, `python-dateutil` and `urllib3`, and no matching lock records for those are shown. It also re-adds `aiohttp = false`, `aiohttp-socks = false` and `hindsight-client = false` to `[options.exclude-newer-package]` and re-sorts that block by hand. The merge commit had already taken the stable-side exclusion block with manual reordering, and only `hindsight-client` was added on the pyproject side in this diff. `docs/stable-review-proposals.json` says `uv.lock was not assigned and therefore was not edited` and lists the lock repair under `decisions_needed`. The merge report instead says the lock was generated by CI. Nothing shown proves `uv lock --check` passes, and the `--locked` sync in stable-integration.yml will fail if pyproject and lock disagree.
findings.fix: Regenerate the lock with uv 0.12.13 (`uv lock`) from the merged pyproject.toml. Do not hand-write package records. Confirm the lock's exclude-newer-package set matches pyproject `[tool.uv]` exactly, including the aiohttp, aiohttp-socks and hindsight-client entries. Confirm transitive packages for hindsight-client exist. Commit the generated lock and gate the merge on a real `uv lock --check` / `uv sync --locked` CI result.

findings.evidence: This scratch artifact has `"status": "decision_needed"` and unresolved `decisions_needed`. Its proposed prompt_builder edit keys the cache on `str(get_hermes_home())`, but the code that landed uses `hermes_home_key()`. Its notes claim the regression tests verify v3 snapshot invalidation and cross-home isolation, but the tests do not discriminate those properties (see the test_prompt_builder.py finding). Keeping it in the tree documents a state that does not match the code.
findings.fix: Delete it from the merge branch, or move its content into the PR description after reconciling it with the actual code and decisions.

findings.evidence: In `_build_skills_system_prompt_inner`, both `app_gated` and `app_availability` are derived only from snapshot entries (local skills dir). Skills from trusted project dirs and external dirs are gated through `_parse_skill_file` -> `skill_matches_apps` during a build, and the result is then cached under a key that carries no app state for them. If an external or project skill declares `requires_apps` and app availability changes, the cached prompt keeps the stale offer decision; it fails open for an app that became unavailable. The new comment claims app availability is part of the key. Also, whenever a snapshot is non-gated, `app_availability` is just all-True names, so it adds nothing beyond 'snapshot present'.
findings.fix: Either compute app gating across project and external entries too (skip the cache read if any visible entry from any tier has `requires_apps`), or include per-tier app decisions in the key. Add a regression with an external-dir skill that has `requires_apps` and toggles availability between two builds.

findings.evidence:
The new regressions do not isolate the behavior they claim to test.
(1) `test_v3_snapshot_without_requires_apps_is_rebuilt_and_gated` builds the manifest from `tmp_path/skills/tools`, but `build_skills_system_prompt()` uses `get_skills_dir()` = `tmp_path/skills`. The manifest keys differ, so the v3 snapshot is rejected on manifest mismatch regardless of the version bump.
(2) `test_profile_snapshot_identity_prevents_cross_home_cache_reuse`: the first build has no snapshot, so its key holds `app_availability=None`. The second key differs anyway, so the test passes even without `hermes_home_key()`. It also assumes the first build creates `home_a` before writing the snapshot, while `home_b` is created explicitly.
(3) `test_prominent_root_config_change_rebuilds_cached_prompt` and `test_app_availability_change_rebuilds_cached_snapshot` likewise pass because of the None->tuple key change or the pre-existing `app_gated` bypass, not the new keying.
(4) The prominent-root test rewrites config.yaml with same-length content ('alpha' vs 'beta'). `_load_raw_config` is cached by `file_signature`, so a coarse mtime could serve the stale config and cause flakiness.
findings.fix: Build the v3 manifest from the same dir the code uses (`tmp_path/'skills'`) so only the version differs, and assert the manifest matches. For home isolation, prime the cache with a valid snapshot in both homes, call twice per home, and assert no cross-home hit (for example, by spying on `_render_skills_index`). For prominent roots, warm the cache with a snapshot present before changing config, and make the config rewrite change size or call `_raw_config_cache_clear()`.
